security_controls.evidence: Conductor approval decisions require trusted harness grant records, packet/risk/type matching, active lifecycle state, hard-stop checks, and verified_by_harness evidence prerequisites. Planner delegated approval execution is rejected.
Human direct approval requires trusted_human_decision and the same hard-stop evidence checks; worker output cannot create approval authority.
Codex and Claude Code surfaces are recorded as replaceable provider examples. Conductor selection does not grant approval authority and does not make provider identity a product dependency.
Entry-file generation validates initialized-project paths and rejects approval-bypass text. Provider execution readiness rejects unsafe command descriptors before CLI readiness is granted.
Adapter artifact validation resolves real paths before trusted-root comparison. A symlink escape regression exists and is skipped only when the Windows host cannot create symlinks.
Conductor ledger events persist selection, entry metadata, delegation grants, routing decisions, worker output refs, adjudication, and approval decisions as queryable read-model records.
Worker output refs and adjudication records are evidence/read-model data only. They do not mutate canonical approval state or become truth claims.

residual_risk: PKT-07 does not execute real Codex CLI or Claude Code CLI processes. Future packets that add process launch behavior must repeat security review for executable allowlists, cwd isolation, timeout/cancel behavior, non-interactive capture, and provider local terms.
Windows symlink escape coverage is present but skipped when the current host lacks symlink creation privileges.
